rules.effective_date_basis: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment
rules.title: Restrictions on criminal-record screening in rental housing
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or consider most criminal history until after making a conditional offer, and even then may consider only specified convictions within stated lookback periods or specified serious offenses. Providers must disclose criminal-history screening before taking an application fee, give reasons and an appeal opportunity if withdrawing an offer, avoid discriminatory criminal-record advertisements, and may not require drug or alcohol tests or drug-abuse-treatment information.
rules.key_value: Conditional offer required before criminal-record inquiry; lookbacks include 6 years for first-degree indictable offenses, 4 years for second- or third-degree, and 1 year for fourth-degree

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to a dwelling unit offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
coverage.summary: Applies statewide to residential rental dwelling units, excluding units in owner-occupied premises with four or fewer dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Before a conditional offer, a provider may consider whether the applicant has ever been convicted of drug-related criminal activity for manufacture or production of methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime State sex-offender registration requirement. The definition of rental dwelling unit excludes owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Violations are enforced through the Division on Civil Rights; penalties may be up to $1,000 for no prior violation within five years, up to $5,000 for one other violation within five years, and up to $10,000 for two or more other violations within seven years. The director may also order cease-and-desist, compliance reporting, possible remedial housing offer, return of application fee, and payment to the applicant up to $1,000.
rules.interaction: The act states that nothing in it bars or affects independent rights or actions, including rights under P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-1 et seq.).
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
